issues.display_title: Issue #221: Emergency Email Magic Link Request API
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Emergency Email Magic Link Request API

Files Changed / Added

  • src/action/v1/auth/magicLink.go (implements RequestMagicLink action handler)
  • src/action/v1/auth/magicLink_test.go (unit tests covering request validation, rate limiting, unregistered email, and email dispatch)
  • src/controllers/v1/authController.go (controller mapping for RequestMagicLink)
  • src/routes/v1/authRoutes.go (registered POST /auth/magic-link/request)
  • src/routes/v1/route.go (added route to middleware.AuthJWTExclude)
  • src/lib/mailer/templates/MagicLink.html (responsive email HTML template with GoThru branding)
  • src/lib/mailer/templates.go (added RenderStandaloneTemplate and EmailTemplateMagicLink)
  • src/workers/email.go (added MAGIC_LINK payload handler in EmailWorker)
  • api-collection/Villume GO/Auth/Request Magic Link.yml (Bruno API collection request)

Summary of Implementation

Implemented the POST /v1/auth/magic-link/request endpoint for the first stage of the Emergency Magic Link Fallback flow during GoThru Keycloak SSO outages:

  1. Email Syntax & Account Verification:

    • Validates that the input is a valid email string.
    • Queries users table using LOWER(email).
    • If the user does not exist, returns 400 Bad Request with code: "unregistered" and messages: "Register First".
    • Inactive accounts (is_active = false) are permitted to proceed, as verification will reactivate them upon inbox confirmation.

  2. Rate Limiting via Redis:

    • Limits magic link requests to 3 requests per 15 minutes per email address using Redis key {prefix}:magic_link:rate:{email}.
    • Returns 429 Too Many Requests when the limit is reached.

  3. Cryptographic Nonce & JWT Token:

    • Generates a 32-byte cryptographic random hex string (nonce).
    • Saves the nonce in Redis with a 15-minute TTL mapped to the user's email ({prefix}:magic_link:nonce:{nonce}).
    • Signs an HMAC-SHA256 JWT using JWT_SECRET containing sub: user.Email, nonce: nonce, type: "magic_link", and 15-minute expiration. No internal user UUIDs are exposed in the link.

  4. URL Formation & Email Worker Dispatch:

    • Dynamically constructs the magic link URL using the WEB_VILLUME_URL environment variable: 
      {WEB_VILLUME_URL}auth/magic-link/verify?token=<token>
    • Publishes an asynchronous message to the RabbitMQ email queue (queues.MailQueue()).
    • The email worker renders MagicLink.html and sends the sign-in notification to the user's email address.

  5. Uniform Response Envelope:

    • Returns a standard 200 OK JSON response using "messages", without redundant keys.

API Example Usage

1. Using cURL

Request:

curl -X POST "https://api-dev.villume.com/v1/auth/magic-link/request" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "email": "user@example.com"
     }'

Success Response (200 OK):

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "If this email is registered, a magic login link has been sent."
  }
}

Error: Unregistered Email (400 Bad Request):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "messages": "Register First",
    "valid": true,
    "code": "unregistered"
  }
}

Error: Rate Limit Exceeded (429 Too Many Requests):

{
  "statusCode": 429,
  "data": {
    "status": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "messages": "Too many magic link requests. Please wait a few minutes before trying again."
    }
  }
}

2. Using TypeScript / Axios (Frontend Integration)

import axios, { AxiosError } from 'axios';

interface RequestMagicLinkResponse {
  statusCode: number;
  data: {
    valid: boolean;
    messages: string;
  };
}

interface ErrorResponse {
  statusCode: number;
  data: {
    code?: string;
    messages?: string;
    errors?: {
      messages?: string;
      input?: string;
    };
  };
}

export async function requestEmergencyMagicLink(email: string): Promise<string> {
  try {
    const response = await axios.post<RequestMagicLinkResponse>(
      `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/v1/auth/magic-link/request`,
      { email }
    );

    return response.data.data.messages;
  } catch (err) {
    const error = err as AxiosError<ErrorResponse>;
    if (error.response) {
      const { status, data } = error.response;

      if (status === 400 && data.data?.code === 'unregistered') {
        throw new Error('This email is not registered yet. Please sign up first.');
      }

      if (status === 429) {
        throw new Error(data.data?.errors?.messages || 'Too many attempts. Please wait 15 minutes.');
      }

      throw new Error(data.data?.errors?.messages || data.data?.messages || 'Failed to request magic link.');
    }

    throw new Error('Network error. Please check your internet connection.');
  }
}

3. Using Fetch API (JavaScript)

async function sendMagicLink(email) {
  const response = await fetch('https://api-dev.villume.com/v1/auth/magic-link/request', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ email }),
  });

  const payload = await response.json();

  if (!response.ok) {
    if (response.status === 400 && payload.data?.code === 'unregistered') {
      alert('Email not found. Please register first.');
      return;
    }
    alert(payload.data?.errors?.messages || payload.data?.messages || 'Error occurred');
    return;
  }

  alert(payload.data.messages);
}

Overview

Implement the POST /v1/auth/magic-link/request endpoint to serve as the first stage of the Emergency Email Magic Link Fallback flow during GoThru Keycloak SSO outages.

When GoThru Keycloak is down or unreachable, standard SSO authentication (POST /v1/auth/gothru and POST /v1/register/gothru) returns 502 Bad Gateway. The client detects this condition and transitions users to the emergency fallback login by requesting their registered email address. This endpoint validates the account, creates a secure single-use temporary token, stores a security nonce in Redis, and dispatches a magic login link to the user's email inbox via RabbitMQ.

Requirements

  1. Public Endpoint & Route Registration:

    • Must be publicly accessible without requiring an existing session token.
    • Registered under POST /v1/auth/magic-link/request.
    • Excluded from JWT middleware via middleware.AuthJWTExclude.

  2. Input Validation:

    • Accepts a JSON payload: {"email": "user@example.com"}.
    • If the request body is malformed JSON, returns 400 Bad Request with "Invalid request body".
    • If the email is missing or empty, returns 400 Bad Request with "Email is required|email".
    • Validates email syntax using net/mail.ParseAddress. Rejects invalid formats with 422 Unprocessable Entity ("Invalid email address format|email").

  3. Account Existence Check:

    • Queries the local database for an existing user where LOWER(email) = LOWER(input).
    • If the account does not exist, returns 400 Bad Request with code: "unregistered" and messages: "Register First".
    • Inactive accounts (is_active = false) are permitted to request magic links as long as they are registered; activation and email verification are completed upon clicking the verified link.

  4. Rate Limiting:

    • Protected against email abuse via Redis rate limiting: maximum of 3 requests per 15 minutes per email.
    • Redis key format: {prefix}:magic_link:rate:{email}.
    • Returns 429 Too Many Requests ("Too many magic link requests. Please wait a few minutes before trying again.") when exceeded.

  5. Cryptographic Nonce & Token Generation:

    • Generates a 32-byte cryptographically secure random nonce (64 hex characters).
    • Stores the nonce in Redis mapped to the user's email with a 15-minute TTL ({prefix}:magic_link:nonce:{nonce}).
    • Generates an HMAC-SHA256 JWT using JWT_SECRET with 15-minute expiration:
      • sub: user's email
      • nonce: generated nonce
      • type: "magic_link"
      • iat: current UTC timestamp
      • exp: timestamp 15 minutes in the future

  6. URL Construction & Email Queueing:

    • Reads WEB_VILLUME_URL from environment variables, ensuring proper trailing slash handling.
    • Constructs the verification link: 
      {WEB_VILLUME_URL}auth/magic-link/verify?token=<url-encoded-jwt>
    • Publishes an email job to RabbitMQ queue queues.MailQueue():
      • type: "MAGIC_LINK"
      • to: user's email
      • subject: "Sign in to GoThru"
      • data: contains email, magic_link_url, link, and expires_in_minutes: 15.
    • Employs the responsive HTML email template MagicLink.html (featuring GoThru branding, a direct sign-in button, fallback copy-paste link, and security notice).

  7. Success Response:

    • Returns uniform 200 OK envelope using messages: 
      {
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "If this email is registered, a magic login link has been sent."
  }
}

Scope

In scope:

  • src/action/v1/auth/magicLink.go (RequestMagicLink action handler)
  • src/action/v1/auth/magicLink_test.go (unit tests covering validation, rate limiting, unregistered email, and success)
  • src/controllers/v1/authController.go (RequestMagicLink controller wrapper)
  • src/routes/v1/authRoutes.go (route definition under /auth/magic-link/request)
  • src/routes/v1/route.go (public exclusion in AuthJWTExclude)
  • src/lib/mailer/templates/MagicLink.html (email HTML template)
  • src/lib/mailer/templates.go (EmailTemplateMagicLink rendering helper)
  • src/workers/email.go (MAGIC_LINK payload handling in EmailWorker)
  • api-collection/Villume GO/Auth/Request Magic Link.yml (Bruno API collection)

API Specification

Request Body

Success Response (200 OK)

400 Bad Request — Missing Email

    "status": "BAD_REQUEST",

    "errors": {
      "messages": "Email is required",
      "input": "email"
    }
  }
}

issues.display_title: Issue #222: Emergency Email Magic Link Verify & Login API
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Emergency Email Magic Link Verify & Login API

Files Changed / Added

  • src/action/v1/auth/magicLink.go (implements VerifyMagicLink action handler)
  • src/action/v1/auth/magicLink_test.go (unit tests covering missing token, expired token, invalid signature, consumed nonce, email verification upgrade, and login finalization)
  • src/controllers/v1/authController.go (controller mapping for VerifyMagicLink)
  • src/routes/v1/authRoutes.go (registered GET /auth/magic-link/verify)
  • src/routes/v1/route.go (added route to middleware.AuthJWTExclude)
  • api-collection/Villume GO/Auth/Verify Magic Link.yml (Bruno API collection request)

Summary of Implementation

Implemented the GET /v1/auth/magic-link/verify endpoint for the second and final stage of the Emergency Magic Link Fallback flow:

  1. Parameter Handling:

    • Parameter is accepted strictly via URL query string (?token=...).
    • Rejects empty tokens with 400 Bad Request ("Token is required|token").

  2. Cryptographic Signature & Nonce Verification:

    • Validates the HMAC-SHA256 signature using JWT_SECRET.
    • Validates that the token has not expired (>15 minutes) and that claim type == "magic_link".
    • Extracts the nonce claim and queries Redis.
    • Anti-Replay Burning: The single-use nonce is immediately deleted (DEL) from Redis upon retrieval. If the nonce was already used or is missing, returns 400 Bad Request ("Magic link has already been used or has expired").
    • Validates that the subject email (sub) matches the email registered to the nonce.

  3. Automatic Email Verification (is_email_verified):

    • Resolves the local account in CockroachDB/PostgreSQL by verified email.
    • If is_email_verified is false, it is automatically updated to true in the database, because clicking the verified email link directly proves ownership of the email inbox.
    • Inactive accounts (is_active = false) are automatically activated (is_active = true).

  4. Session Finalization & Standard Manual Login Response:

    • Calls finalizeLogin(c, user, resolveLoginType(user.Email)) — canceling any pending delete requests and updating last_login.
    • Returns the exact identical response format as Villume's manual login: 
      {
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Login success",
    "status": "OK",
    "token": "<villume-session-jwt>",
    "username": "<username>",
    "is_email_verified": true,
    "is_welcome": true,
    "exp": 1729000000
  }
}

API Example Usage

1. Using cURL

Request:

curl -X GET "https://api-dev.villume.com/v1/auth/magic-link/verify?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."

Success Response (200 OK):

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Login success",
    "status": "OK",
    "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJleHAiOjE3NjI5MDAwMDAsImlhdCI6MTc2MDI5MDAwMCwibHMiOiIyMDI2LTEwLTE5VDEyOjAwOjAwIiwicm9sZSI6InVzZXIiLCJzdWIiOiJkR1Z6ZEM1aFkybHVaUT09In0.ABC123xyz...",
    "username": "johndoe",
    "is_email_verified": true,
    "is_welcome": true,
    "exp": 1762900000
  }
}

Error: Expired or Invalid Token (400 Bad Request):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "status": "BAD_REQUEST",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "messages": "Magic link is invalid or has expired"
    }
  }
}

Error: Already Used Link / Nonce Consumed (400 Bad Request):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "status": "BAD_REQUEST",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "messages": "Magic link has already been used or has expired"
    }
  }
}

2. Next.js / React Frontend Integration Example

This example demonstrates how a Next.js / React page (e.g., app/auth/magic-link/verify/page.tsx) consumes the link when clicked by the user:

'use client';

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { useSearchParams, useRouter } from 'next/navigation';
import axios from 'axios';

interface VerifyLoginResponse {
  statusCode: number;
  data: {
    valid: boolean;
    messages: string;
    status: string;
    token: string;
    username: string;
    is_email_verified: boolean;
    is_welcome: boolean;
    exp: number;
  };
}

export default function MagicLinkVerifyPage() {
  const searchParams = useSearchParams();
  const router = useRouter();
  const [errorMessage, setErrorMessage] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [isVerifying, setIsVerifying] = useState(true);

  useEffect(() => {
    const token = searchParams.get('token');

    if (!token) {
      setErrorMessage('Verification token is missing.');
      setIsVerifying(false);
      return;
    }

    async function verifyAndAuthenticate() {
      try {
        const response = await axios.get<VerifyLoginResponse>(
          `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/v1/auth/magic-link/verify`,
          {
            params: { token },
          }
        );

        const { token: sessionJwt } = response.data.data;

        // Store session token in localStorage / cookie
        localStorage.setItem('token', sessionJwt);

        // Redirect user to dashboard
        router.push('/dashboard');
      } catch (err: any) {
        const message =
          err.response?.data?.data?.errors?.messages ||
          err.response?.data?.data?.messages ||
          'Failed to verify magic link. It may have expired or already been used.';
        setErrorMessage(message);
        setIsVerifying(false);
      }
    }

    verifyAndAuthenticate();
  }, [searchParams, router]);

  if (isVerifying) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col items-center justify-center min-h-screen">
        <h1 className="text-xl font-semibold mb-2">Verifying Magic Link...</h1>
        <p className="text-gray-500">Signing you into your account, please wait.</p>
      </div>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center justify-center min-h-screen text-center p-4">
      <h1 className="text-xl font-bold text-red-600 mb-2">Sign In Failed</h1>
      <p className="text-gray-700 mb-6">{errorMessage}</p>
      <a
        href="/login"
        className="px-6 py-2 bg-indigo-900 text-white rounded-full font-medium hover:bg-indigo-800"
      >
        Back to Sign In
      </a>
    </div>
  );
}

3. Using TypeScript Function (Axios)

import axios from 'axios';

export async function verifyMagicLinkToken(token: string): Promise<string> {
  const response = await axios.get(
    `https://api-dev.villume.com/v1/auth/magic-link/verify`,
    {
      params: { token },
    }
  );

  // Returns the standard 30-day Villume session JWT
  return response.data.data.token;
}

Overview

Implement the GET /v1/auth/magic-link/verify endpoint to serve as the second and final stage of the Emergency Email Magic Link Fallback flow during GoThru Keycloak SSO outages.

When the user receives the magic login link in their email inbox, clicking the link redirects their browser to the verification endpoint with the query parameter ?token=.... This endpoint validates the cryptographic signature and expiration of the token, consumes and deletes the single-use nonce from Redis to prevent replay attacks, resolves the local user account, automatically promotes unverified accounts to is_email_verified = true, terminates any pending deletion requests, and issues a standard 30-day Villume session token with the identical payload returned by Villume's manual login.

Requirements

  1. Public Endpoint & Route Registration:

    • Must be publicly accessible without requiring an existing session token.
    • Registered strictly under GET /v1/auth/magic-link/verify.
    • Excluded from JWT middleware via middleware.AuthJWTExclude.
    • Does not accept POST or request body payloads; parameters are provided strictly via URL query string.

  2. Parameter Validation:

    • Accepts a single query parameter: ?token=<token>.
    • If token is missing or empty, returns 400 Bad Request with "Token is required|token".

  3. Cryptographic Token & Nonce Verification:

    • Validates the token's HMAC-SHA256 signature and expiration using JWT_SECRET.
    • If signature verification fails or the token has expired (>15 minutes), returns 400 Bad Request ("Magic link is invalid or has expired").
    • Validates claim type == "magic_link". If mismatch, returns 400 Bad Request ("Invalid token type").
    • Validates claim nonce. If missing, returns 400 Bad Request ("Missing token nonce").
    • Single-use nonce verification via Redis:
      • Retrieves the email associated with the nonce.
      • Immediately deletes (DEL) the nonce key from Redis to prevent replay attacks.
      • If the nonce is missing, expired, or already used, returns 400 Bad Request ("Magic link has already been used or has expired").
    • Confirms that the email inside the JWT claim (sub) matches the email bound to the Redis nonce.

  4. User Resolution & Automatic Email Verification:

    • Queries the local database for the user account by verified email (LOWER(email)).
    • If the account does not exist, returns 404 Not Found ("User account not found").
    • Automatic Email Verification: If is_email_verified is currently false, the system automatically updates is_email_verified = true in the database, because clicking the verified email link directly proves ownership of the email inbox.
    • If the account was marked is_active = false, it is automatically reactivated (is_active = true).

  5. Session Finalization & Standard Response:

    • Calls finalizeLogin with resolveLoginType(user.Email):
      • Cancels pending deletion requests (models.UsersRequestDelete).
      • Updates last_login timestamp in the database.
      • Issues a standard 30-day Villume session JWT.
    • Returns the exact identical response envelope and data structure as Villume's manual login: 
      {
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Login success",
    "status": "OK",
    "token": "<villume-session-jwt>",
    "username": "<username>",
    "is_email_verified": true,
    "is_welcome": true,
    "exp": 1729000000
  }
}

Scope

In scope:

  • src/action/v1/auth/magicLink.go (VerifyMagicLink action handler)
  • src/action/v1/auth/magicLink_test.go (unit tests covering missing token, expired token, invalid signature, consumed nonce, unverified user promotion, and login success)
  • src/controllers/v1/authController.go (VerifyMagicLink controller wrapper)
  • src/routes/v1/authRoutes.go (route definition GET /auth/magic-link/verify)
  • src/routes/v1/route.go (public exclusion in AuthJWTExclude)
  • api-collection/Villume GO/Auth/Verify Magic Link.yml (Bruno API collection)

API Specification
